key_insight: BLT-D adds a block-wise diffusion objective to the Byte Latent Transformer, enabling block-parallel generation that is substantially faster than byte-by-byte autoregressive sampling while retaining next-byte prediction quality.
problem_solved: Byte-level LMs are bottlenecked by slow autoregressive byte-by-byte generation; this work speeds up sampling without sacrificing the benefits of tokenization-free modeling.
method: Introduce BLT-D: augment the Byte Latent Transformer with an auxiliary block-wise diffusion objective during training.
Train jointly with the standard next-byte prediction loss so the model preserves autoregressive language modeling quality.
Use a block-wise (partially parallel) generation procedure that samples groups of bytes via the learned latent/diffusion mechanism to reduce sampling latency.
impact: Provides a practical, low-latency way to deploy tokenization-free byte-level LMs, improving throughput for multilingual and robust NLP applications while keeping model behavior comparable to standard next-byte LMs.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing generation speed (tokens/sec or wall-clock latency) of byte-by-byte BLT vs BLT-D vs token-level baselines
Architecture diagram highlighting latent blocks, the diffusion auxiliary objective, and the next-byte prediction head
Flowchart contrasting byte-by-byte autoregressive sampling with BLT-D block-wise sampling (showing parallelism gains)
Latency vs quality (perplexity or accuracy) curve to show trade-off and that BLT-D maintains LM performance while reducing latency
paper_authors: Julie Kallini, Artidoro Pagnoni, Tomasz Limisiewicz, Gargi Ghosh, Luke Zettlemoyer
